title: 23.8 An 88.36TOPS/W Bit-Level-Weight-Compressed Large-Language-Model Accelerator with Cluster-Aligned INT-FP-GEMM and Bi-Dimensional Workflow Reformulation
problem: Large language model inference deployment faces three orthogonal challenges: (1) autoregressive generation requires 1000x more external memory accesses (EMA) per token vs. non-autoregressive transformers due to streaming weight reads and KV-cache updates; (2) mixed-precision (INT-FP) GEMM with quantized weights and FP activations typically requires dequantization overhead (4.6x power vs. native INT-FP), reducing quantization benefits; (3) special function units (softmax, trigonometric) create compute-memory coupling where processors wait 1/3 of time for SFU results.
motivation: Cloud and edge AI deployment of large LLMs demands energy efficiency; accelerators optimized for traditional transformers fail to address LLM-specific bottlenecks.
method: Dedicated LLM accelerator employing three innovations: (1) bit-level weight compression with efficient INT-FP mixed-precision GEMM avoiding dequantization overhead while preserving quantization benefits; (2) cluster-aligned processing enabling efficient data movement and tiling across compressed weight formats; (3) bi-dimensional workflow reformulation decoupling GEMM and SFU operations, allowing PEs to continue while SFU processes non-linear functions asynchronously, eliminating PE stalls. Architecture optimizes for LLM memory-access patterns and compute-intensive non-linear operations.
key_novelty: Cluster-aligned INT-FP-GEMM with bi-dimensional workflow decoupling GEMM and SFU computation eliminating PE stalls in LLM inference.
contributions: 88.36 TOPS/W energy efficiency for LLM inference
Bit-level weight compression with native INT-FP-GEMM (avoiding dequantization)
Cluster-aligned processing for efficient tiling and data movement
Bi-dimensional workflow decoupling SFU from GEMM (eliminates PE stalls)
baselines: prior LLM accelerators without workflow optimization
limitations: Abstract does not provide model sizes tested, latency metrics, memory bandwidth requirements, die area, power consumption absolute values, or head-to-head comparison with state-of-art LLM accelerators (e.g., TPU v5, H100).
primary_theme: LLM inference accelerator with cluster-aligned INT-FP-GEMM and workflow decoupling
